----------------------------------------------------------------------
PROJECT NARRATIVE (SUBMITTED BY APPLICANT)
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Happy Tots Learning Centre has operated a half-day preschool
programme in the Jalan Besar area since 2019. Our centre serves a
community where many families face financial constraints, and where
access to early literacy support is limited. We have observed in our
own classrooms that children who struggle with early reading skills
often fall further behind once they enter primary school, and our
teachers have repeatedly requested additional resources to support
these children.

The Early Literacy Enrichment project is designed to meet this need.
The project will operate two afternoons per week, with each session
serving a group of 15–20 children. Sessions will be led by trained
literacy facilitators and will include:

- Shared reading activities using high-quality picture books
- Phonics games and letter-sound recognition exercises
- Small-group guided reading
- Home lending library, allowing children to take books home

In addition to the direct literacy instruction, the project will
engage parents through quarterly workshops on supporting reading at
home. We believe that parental involvement is essential to sustained
literacy gains, and we have built these workshops into the programme
design.

The centre has secured a letter of support from the principal of
Kallang Primary School, who has agreed to share baseline and
follow-up reading data for children who transition from our programme
to the school. This will allow us to measure the project's impact
beyond the immediate programme period.

We are requesting SGD 48,500 from the Community Impact Fund to
support the full 12 months of implementation. We are confident that
the project is well-designed, feasible, and responsive to a clear
community need.

The first tranche of SGD 22,500 (50% of the approved amount) will be disbursed upon receipt of the signed acceptance form and the completed disbursement request form. The remaining SGD 22,500 will be disbursed upon satisfactory review of the interim progress report.

This memo updates the documentation standards for grant applications received from Cycle 2023 onwards. The purpose of this revision is to reduce discrepancies in file organisation, improve audit readiness, and ensure consistency across reviewer handoffs.

Effective immediately, please observe the following:

1. **Application File Cover Page.** A standard cover page (template attached) shall be affixed to the front of every physical and digital application file. The cover page must include the application ID, applicant name, project title, date received, and the assigned Grants Officer. Any subsequent change in officer assignment must be recorded on the cover page under “Change of Officer” with the date.

2. **Supporting Documents Checklist.** Every application must include a completed Supporting Documents Checklist (template attached). This checklist must be signed and dated by the reviewing officer upon verification of each item. Incomplete checklists will be returned to the applicant’s file and flagged in the status log as “Pending Documents” until resolved.

3. **Review Process Flowchart.** A flowchart describing the review process is attached for reference. Please note that the flowchart supersedes the previous version circulated in April 2022. Key changes include the introduction of a preliminary eligibility screen at Week 2 and a mandatory second review for applications requesting above $80,000.

4. **Record Retention.** All records, including superseded versions of application forms, must be retained for a minimum of five years from the date of final decision. Superseded documents should be marked with a diagonal stamp reading “SUPERSEDED” and kept in the file’s “Historical” section, not discarded.

5. **Naming Conventions.** Digital files must follow the naming convention: `APP-YYYY-NNN_ApplicantName_YYYYMMDD`. For example, `APP-2023-012_TanAiLing_20230115.pdf`. Physical files should be labelled with the same application ID and applicant name.

Please direct any questions regarding these standards to the Grants Office Manager.

PROJECT NARRATIVE (SUBMITTED BY APPLICANT)
----------------------------------------------------------------------

Happy Tots Learning Centre has operated a half-day preschool
programme in the Jalan Besar area since 2019. Our centre serves a
community where many families face financial constraints, and where
access to early literacy support is limited. We have observed in our
own classrooms that children who struggle with early reading skills
often fall further behind once they enter primary school, and our
teachers have repeatedly requested additional resources to support
these children.

The Early Literacy Enrichment project is designed to meet this need.
The project will operate two afternoons per week, with each session
serving a group of 15–20 children. Sessions will be led by trained
literacy facilitators and will include:

- Shared reading activities using high-quality picture books
- Phonics games and letter-sound recognition exercises
- Small-group guided reading
- Home lending library, allowing children to take books home

In addition to the direct literacy instruction, the project will
engage parents through quarterly workshops on supporting reading at
home. We believe that parental involvement is essential to sustained
literacy gains, and we have built these workshops into the programme
design.

The centre has secured a letter of support from the principal of
Kallang Primary School, who has agreed to share baseline and
follow-up reading data for children who transition from our programme
to the school. This will allow us to measure the project's impact
beyond the immediate programme period.

We are requesting SGD 48,500 from the Community Impact Fund to
support the full 12 months of implementation. We are confident that
the project is well-designed, feasible, and responsive to a clear
community need.

**CIFS GRANTS OFFICE – INTERNAL MEMORANDUM**

**To:** All Grants Office Staff
**From:** Grants Office Manager
**Date:** 3 January 2023
**Re:** Standardisation of Application Records and File Handling

This memo updates the documentation standards for grant applications received from Cycle 2023 onwards. The purpose of this revision is to reduce discrepancies in file organisation, improve audit readiness, and ensure consistency across reviewer handoffs.

Effective immediately, please observe the following:

1. **Application File Cover Page.** A standard cover page (template attached) shall be affixed to the front of every physical and digital application file. The cover page must include the application ID, applicant name, project title, date received, and the assigned Grants Officer. Any subsequent change in officer assignment must be recorded on the cover page under “Change of Officer” with the date.

2. **Supporting Documents Checklist.** Every application must include a completed Supporting Documents Checklist (template attached). This checklist must be signed and dated by the reviewing officer upon verification of each item. Incomplete checklists will be returned to the applicant’s file and flagged in the status log as “Pending Documents” until resolved.

3. **Review Process Flowchart.** A flowchart describing the review process is attached for reference. Please note that the flowchart supersedes the previous version circulated in April 2022. Key changes include the introduction of a preliminary eligibility screen at Week 2 and a mandatory second review for applications requesting above $80,000.

4. **Record Retention.** All records, including superseded versions of application forms, must be retained for a minimum of five years from the date of final decision. Superseded documents should be marked with a diagonal stamp reading “SUPERSEDED” and kept in the file’s “Historical” section, not discarded.

5. **Naming Conventions.** Digital files must follow the naming convention: `APP-YYYY-NNN_ApplicantName_YYYYMMDD`. For example, `APP-2023-012_TanAiLing_20230115.pdf`. Physical files should be labelled with the same application ID and applicant name.

Please direct any questions regarding these standards to the Grants Office Manager.

**1. SERIES DESCRIPTION AND ARCHIVAL NOTE**

This series comprises the official record of applications submitted to the Community Impact Fund of Singapore (CIFS) between 1 January 2022 and 31 December 2025. The series includes application forms, supporting documents, reviewer assessments, correspondence with applicants, and decision letters. The series is arranged chronologically by application year, and within each year, by application reference number.

**1.1 Archival Procedures**

The following procedures apply to the maintenance and eventual transfer of this series to the National Archives of Singapore:

1.  **File Integrity:** No document may be removed from an application file without the written approval of the Grants Director. Any removal must be recorded on a File Removal Slip (Form CIFS-FR-01) and filed in the relevant application folder.
2.  **Access:** Access to application files is restricted to Grants Office staff and members of the Grants Committee. Requests from external parties must be made in writing to the Grants Director and will be assessed in accordance with the Personal Data Protection Act 2012.
3.  **Retention and Disposal:** Upon completion of the retention period, files will be reviewed for archival value. Files not selected for permanent preservation will be destroyed by secure shredding, with a Certificate of Destruction (Form CIFS-CD-01) completed and retained by the Records Officer.
4.  **Transfer to Archives:** At the end of each calendar year, the complete set of closed application files for that year will be transferred to the National Archives of Singapore. A Transfer of Custody Note (see Section 4) will be executed by the Grants Director and the Archives' authorised officer.
5.  **Digital Records:** Scanned copies of all physical documents are stored in the CIFS Grants Management System (GMS). The GMS is the system of record for application status changes. Physical files are stored in the secure records room at the CIFS office, 1 Raffles Place, #20-01, Singapore 048616.

**1.2 Inactive Applications**

Applications that were withdrawn by the applicant or deemed ineligible during the eligibility check are considered inactive. Inactive applications are retained for a period of 3 years from the date of the decision, after which they are destroyed. Inactive applications are not included in the annual transfer to the National Archives.
